Threat.value: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me

Memory.value: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try

vignette: As a child, Alessia had grown accustomed to the sound of her parents' arguments escalating into something more. She would often retreat to her room, covering her ears with pillows in an attempt to drown out the shouting and crashing from downstairs. But one particular night still lingered in her mind like a scar. Her father's rage had spilled over into the kitchen, where her mother stood frozen against the counter as he slammed his fist onto the countertop, mere inches from her face. Alessia, then only 10 years old, had watched in terror from the top of the stairs, unsure whether to intervene or flee. In the aftermath, Alessia's parents continued their volatile relationship, and she learned to navigate this treacherous landscape with caution. As she grew older, however, the memories of that night began to resurface, refusing to be silenced. Some moments remained etched in her mind with vivid clarity – the sound of shattering glass, the look of pure fear on her mother's face – while others were lost to a frustrating fog, no matter how hard she tried to recall them. Alessia now found herself hyper-vigilant in public spaces, scanning crowds for potential threats and gravitating towards areas where she felt safest. As a City Council Member, she often attended community events, but her anxiety was beginning to take its toll on her professional life. She'd become increasingly withdrawn, preferring to stay behind the scenes rather than engage with constituents or give speeches. Her colleagues had begun to notice the change in her demeanor, but Alessia struggled to articulate the source of her distress. When memories of that childhood night resurfaced, Alessia's body would involuntarily reenact the same defensive posture she'd assumed as a child – her shoulders hunched, her weight shifted onto one leg. The physical sensations transported her back to those stairs, reliving the terror and helplessness she felt as a witness to her parents' violence. As Alessia lay in bed at night, her mind racing with worst-case scenarios, sleep eluded her. She would watch her husband sleeping peacefully beside her, feeling a pang of envy for his ability to shut off the world so easily. Her own fears and anxieties had become an exhausting constant companion. Despite her struggles, it was a recent encounter that finally pushed Alessia to seek help. At a community forum, she found herself in close proximity to a man who bore a striking resemblance to her father – same rugged jawline, same imposing stature. The sudden rush of adrenaline and the accompanying memories sent her fleeing from the room, leaving behind a bewildered audience and worried colleagues. As Alessia sat in the therapist's office, recounting this episode for the first time, she realized that her carefully constructed "safe zones" had begun to shrink. Her fear was no longer just about physical harm but also about losing control, becoming the helpless child on those stairs once more. What frightened her most was not the memories themselves but the possibility of unraveling entirely – losing herself in a world where danger lurked around every corner, and she couldn't find solace even in her own home. With each passing day, Alessia felt like she was losing ground to these creeping anxieties, watching as they insidiously seeped into every aspect of her life. She hoped that therapy might offer a way to regain some semblance of control, to slowly rebuild the sense of security and safety she so desperately craved.
